review.comment: Good use of compound assignment and a done branch; totals compute correctly when input is valid. Invalid score and operation paths never print ERROR to stdout, Number.isFinite is applied to the string line, and extra per-line logs break acceptance output. Next: parse line 1 with Number(), validate the number, console.log errors, and print only Total on done.

Compound assignments and the done total work for valid input sequences. Initial score never rejects non-numeric lines because Number.isFinite is checked on the string, and malformed ops print ERROR: invalid score instead of invalid operation, then still print Total. Next: parse line 1 with Number(), validate Number.isFinite(score), use ERROR: invalid operation for bad ops, and return after each error.

Compound assignments work for valid sequences and both Total examples pass. abc produces no error because Number.isFinite is checked on the string line before score is parsed, and +x prints ERROR: invalid score instead of ERROR: invalid operation. Next: on line 1 use score = Number(line) then if (!Number.isFinite(score)) print ERROR: invalid score and return.

Compound assignments handle valid sequences well; Total outputs and +x invalid-operation errors match the README. Invalid first lines like abc produce no output because the score guard uses operator==0 instead of an else after Number.isFinite fails. Next: after parsing line 1, if !Number.isFinite(Number(line)), log ERROR: invalid score and return.
Compound operators apply sequences correctly; Total and both ERROR messages match the README. Number.isFinite validates the initial score and operation operands. Solid match to acceptance criteria.
